title: Mandate (with committed semantic baseline)
description: §3. The base payment mandate: 'a stored, cryptographically signed mandate derived from a natural-language instruction' (Abstract), extended with the §3 committed baseline and pinned scoring stack, the §4.4 patch-chain governance parameters, the §5.2 freshness terms, and the §6 challenge and presentation policy. §9: 'the MandatePatch and supersession lineage extend those mandate formats with a small set of additional fields and one registry obligation' — this schema is a standalone rendering of that field set, not a replacement for AP2 or Verifiable Intent mandates.

canonicalization_profile.description: §4.3: 'each binding profile MUST define the deterministic serialization and hash encoding that make the commitment byte-identical across parties.' PROFILE-DEFINED: the paper fixes no serialization; this repository ships `mandatepatch/profile/v1`.

binding_profile.description: §9: 'Bindings for AP2, Verifiable Intent, and ACP are sketched in the artifact archive published alongside this disclosure.' Identifier of the mandate format this artifact binds to. PROFILE-DEFINED.

mandate_family_id.description: §5.3, 'The mandate family's home registry — wallet or issuer — is the sole linearizable consume authority.' Stable identifier of the family across all versions.

mandate_version.description: §5.1. Monotonic version within the family; supersession lineage is over versions.

supersedes.description: §5.1, 'supersedes = H(previous) lineage over signed natural-language mandates, in which amendment carries semantic re-baselining — a new committed E₀ — and not merely parameter change.' Explicit null for the first version of a family.

epoch.description: §5.2, §7. Supersession epoch at which this version became family head; 'the epoch head enter[s] the statement as a public input' (§7). §5.2: 'An authorization is valid only with a freshness proof that its mandate version was the family head at an epoch not older than a mandate-specified staleness bound Δ.'

instruction.description: §3.1: 'Both the immutable source bytes of the instruction and its canonical machine interpretation are signed at mandate creation, and material conflicts between them are surfaced at approval time.'

source_text.description: §3.1, 'the immutable source bytes of the instruction'. The natural-language instruction as given, e.g. the worked example's 'groceries from the usual store, the usual staples including a twelve-pack of a named soft drink, capped at $150' (§1).

source_bytes_hash.description: §3.1. Hash over the immutable source bytes, so the signed bytes are identifiable without disclosing them.

machine_interpretation.description: §3.1, 'its canonical machine interpretation'. The structured reading of the instruction that the predicate set encodes. PROFILE-DEFINED: the interpretation vocabulary — this repository does not fix one.

machine_interpretation_hash.description: §3.1. Hash over the canonical machine interpretation.

surfaced_conflicts.description: §3.1, 'material conflicts between them are surfaced at approval time'; §8: 'Divergence between what the instruction's bytes say and what the machine interpretation encodes is answered by signing both and surfacing conflicts at approval.' Empty array when none were found — never omitted.

source_excerpt.description: The instruction text in tension with the interpretation.

note.description: What was shown to the principal at approval.

semantic_gate.description: §3. The committed baseline and the terms under which divergence is scored. §3.1 states the five residuals this object carries: a committed rather than stored baseline, a pinned scoring stack inside the principal-signed artifact, suspension rather than decline, a signed divergence record per evaluation, and scoring welded to the canonical transaction commitment.

baseline_commitment.description: §3.1, first residual: 'the baseline is committed, not stored. At mandate signing time the wallet computes an embedding E₀ of the normalized instruction under a pinned scoring stack and places commit(E₀) = H(E₀ ‖ salt) — hiding in the random-oracle model, binding under collision resistance — inside the signed mandate, with the salt held by the wallet and revealed only in dispute.' NOTE: this repository ships no scorer. E₀ is produced outside this library; only the commitment is an artifact field.

commitment_scheme.description: §3.1. Identifier of the commitment construction for commit(E₀) = H(E₀ ‖ salt). PROFILE-DEFINED: the paper fixes the property (hiding under ROM, binding under collision resistance), not the construction.

salt_disclosure_policy.description: §3.1, 'with the salt held by the wallet and revealed only in dispute'.

scoring_stack.description: §3.1, second residual: 'the scoring stack is pinned inside the principal-signed artifact. The mandate carries a measurement of the full stack — model hash, tokenizer, normalization rules, preprocessing, quantization, runtime configuration — not a bare model identifier, together with a monotonic stack version that verifiers enforce against rollback ... so that neither a verifier nor an attacker can silently substitute a more permissive scorer.'

stack_measurement.description: §3.1, 'a measurement of the full stack ... not a bare model identifier'. §8: 'scoring-stack substitution [is answered] by whole-stack measurement with anti-rollback on stack versions.'

stack_version.description: §3.1, 'a monotonic stack version that verifiers enforce against rollback'.

quantization.description: §3.1, 'quantization'. Explicit null when the stack is unquantized.

threshold_micro.description: §3.1, 'the threshold τ', in integer millionths. The gate fires when d(E₀, E₁) > τ, where AARM's distance is 'd(r₀,aₙ) = 1 − cosine(embed(r₀), embed(aₙ))' (§3.1); τ = 0.18 is encoded 180000. PROFILE-DEFINED (two decisions): the distance function and its range — profile v1 assumes cosine distance on unit-normalized embeddings, hence [0, 2] — and the numeric encoding, since profile v1 admits integers only in every artifact so that the TypeScript and Python ports cannot diverge on float formatting.

category_taxonomy.description: §3.1, 'the category taxonomy under which τ was selected'. §8: 'Taxonomy and threshold laundering is answered by the pinned taxonomy and most-conservative-category selection carried in the signed mandate.'

threshold_selection_rule.description: §3.1: 'the applicable threshold is always the most conservative among matching categories'.

aggregation.description: §3.1: 'Scoring is performed per line item with worst-case aggregation alongside any cart-level score; authorization never rests on a single cart-centroid embedding, which would permit an out-of-scope item to hide inside an in-scope basket.' §8: 'Semantic averaging is answered by mandatory per-line-item scoring with worst-case aggregation.'

deployment_variant.description: §3.1: 'Three deployment variants are specified with distinct trust properties: wallet-side scoring (private, self-attested), gateway-side scoring (network-visible, requires cart disclosure), and TEE-attested scoring (private and third-party verifiable, with the enclave measurement covering the full pinned stack).'

enclave_measurement.description: §3.1. Required for the TEE-attested variant, 'with the enclave measurement covering the full pinned stack'; explicit null otherwise.

cumulative_divergence_budget_micro.description: §3.2: 'A cumulative divergence budget per mandate across transactions guards against semantic salami slicing, in which many individually-passing transactions drift in aggregate.'

attempt_budget.description: §3.1: 'per-mandate attempt budgets and cart-revision throttling bound iterative probing of the decision boundary.'

agent_visible_outcome_space.description: §3.1: 'The agent-visible outcome is strictly binary — pass or suspend.'

score_disclosure.description: §3.1: 'the numeric score is encrypted to the user and issuer within the divergence record; upstream parties receive coarse reason codes.'

predicates.description: §4.2. The predicate set evaluated de novo on every authorization: 'machine-enforceable constraints, every third-party-pinned predicate, the semantic gate over every line item, cumulative budgets, and the Section 5.2 freshness check'. §1 quotes Verifiable Intent's split between 'machine-enforceable constraints (amount, payee, merchant), verified at execution time, [and] descriptive fields (product name, brand, color, size) that provide informational context only' — the `kind` field records which side a predicate falls on.

allOf.$comment: §4.2: 'Patches amend only principal-owned predicates ... that predicate is unpatchable by the principal.' Encoded as a schema constraint.

predicate_id.description: §4.2. Referenced by a MandatePatch violation tuple's `violated_predicate_id`.

kind.description: §1, §4.2. Which class of predicate this is.

owner.description: §4.2: 'where an issuer, lender, or program has pinned a predicate — a covenant, an eligibility rule, a category restriction — that predicate is unpatchable by the principal'.

patchable.description: §4.2. True only for principal-owned predicates. 'A MandatePatch cannot make a transaction permissible that a third party's independent policy prohibits. This layer is a principal-side meaning check, not an override of anyone else's authority.'

expression.description: The predicate itself, evaluated against the §4.3 canonical commitment. PROFILE-DEFINED: the predicate expression language — this repository fixes none and ships no evaluator.

description.description: Human-readable statement of the predicate, for §6 display.

max_patches_before_forced_supersession.description: §4.4: 'After a low, profile-defined mandatory number of patches, supersession is forced.' PROFILE-DEFINED: the paper says 'low' and 'profile-defined' and fixes no number. The 1–10 bound here is this repository's reading of 'low', not a value from the paper.

cooling_off_seconds.description: §4.4: 'a profile-defined cooling-off interval before a durable expansion can be signed.' PROFILE-DEFINED.

full_context_redisplay_required.description: §4.4: 'because patch-exhaustion supersession arrives precisely when a fatigued user is most exploitable, it requires full-context re-display of the original mandate together with all accumulated deltas'.

base_locked_while_patch_pending.description: §4.4: 'While any patch is pending — the pending state beginning at challenge issuance and ending at patch consumption, challenge expiry, or decline — the base mandate is locked against new authorization requests at the consume authority — the pending challenge and supersession remain available — closing the bypass in which micro-transactions are fired to settlement between patch requests to defeat a pending-only cumulative cap.'

cumulative_scope_budget.description: §4.4: 'A multidimensional cumulative scope budget — semantic distance, monetary delta, merchant-set delta, tracked per axis — governs the chain, extending the cumulative-spend tracking that Verifiable Intent already requires of networks across Layer-3 fulfillments.'

monetary_delta_minor.description: §4.4, axis two, in integer minor units.

merchant_set_delta.description: §4.4, axis three: permitted growth of the merchant set.

staleness_bound_seconds.description: §5.2: 'a mandate-specified staleness bound Δ ... Δ is a service-level bound, not a euphemism: for amendments, activity within Δ against the prior version is tolerated by design.' PROFILE-DEFINED: the value of Δ.

revocation_mode.description: §5.2: 'for revocation, a synchronous-head-check mode with Δ approaching zero is specified, because the realistic adversary is an agent that reads the principal's communications and can front-run an announced revocation within any tolerance window.'

head_source.description: §5.2: 'The transparency-log deployment requires cosigned heads or a witness network against split-view equivocation; the issuer-registry deployment states its single-operator trust plainly.'

cosigned_heads_required.description: §5.2. MUST be true for the transparency-log deployment; §8: 'Split-view equivocation against the transparency-log deployment requires cosigned heads.'

evaluation_points.description: §5.1, §5.2: freshness is 'evaluated both at authorization and again at capture or commit time, on asynchronous rails where no atomic check exists' — 'checked at the authorization's linearization instant and re-checked at capture.'

consume_authority.description: §5.3: 'The mandate family's home registry — wallet or issuer — is the sole linearizable consume authority for patch nullifiers and epoch heads. Cross-rail verifiers check it. Exactly-once patch consumption across heterogeneous rails is achieved by construction at that authority, not assumed of the rails.' §5.2: 'Cross-rail immediate finality is not claimed: the consume authority is the linearization point and rails inherit its consistency.' NOTE: this repository implements no consume authority.

challenge_ttl_seconds.description: §6.1, 'an expiring out-of-band confirmation' (Abstract). PROFILE-DEFINED: the TTL.

expiry_disposition.description: §6.1: 'fail-closed expiry: an expired challenge voids the checkout; nothing silently proceeds or falls back.'

max_outstanding_challenges.description: §6.2: 'Per-mandate caps on outstanding challenges ... bound the duplication attack, which issues fresh valid challenges rather than replays.'

max_candidates_per_challenge.description: §6.2, 'a per-challenge cap on presented candidates'. §8 notes the residual: 'the agent curates which honest alternatives are presented, so choice-architecture steering ... survives even though every candidate's contents are canonically bound and internally consistent; the protocol's answers are the first-class decline-all outcome and candidate-count caps.'

assurance_profile.description: §6.2: 'Authenticator requirements are expressed as assurance profiles — named tiers of authenticator strength and channel independence that a mandate or verifier policy selects by risk.' PROFILE-DEFINED: the tier vocabulary.

device_bound_credential_required.description: §6.2: 'High-risk patches require device-bound credentials or an authenticator independent of the ecosystem controlling the agent session; a registered passkey is the floor, not the profile.'

channel_independence_required.description: §6.2, §8. Whether the authenticator must be independent of the ecosystem controlling the agent session.

decline_all_is_first_class.description: §6.1: 'declining every candidate is a first-class outcome that voids the checkout.'

renderer_profile.description: §6.3: 'Challenge renderings under this disclosure MUST be produced by a renderer meeting [draft-schrock-ep-presentation-binding]'s determinism and neutralization requirements; those properties are adopted here, not claimed.' PROFILE-DEFINED: the renderer identifier and version.

deterministic_rendering_required.description: §6.3: 'a deterministic renderer — a pure function from the signed canonical action to a byte-identical human-readable rendering'.

neutralization_required.description: §6.3: 'normative neutralization of bidirectional overrides, control characters, and homoglyph-bearing runs, refuse-on-unsafe semantics, verifier re-derivation'.

render_state_hash_required.description: §6.3, §4.2. Whether the optional render-state hash is mandatory under this mandate's policy.

minimum_attestation_tier.description: §6.3: 'a tiered attestation level (hardware secure-display, OS-composited, software) is recorded in the artifact, with the software tier declared evidentially weak'.

font_hash.description: §6.3, 'pinned font hash'. Explicit null when no font is pinned.

locale.description: §6.3, 'locale-fixed numeric formatting within that font'. §8 lists 'locale separator confusion' among the display attacks the canonicalization profile answers.

render_to_input_event_binding_required.description: §6.3: 'render-to-input-event binding closes the time-of-check/time-of-use window between display and confirmation.'

expiry.description: Mandate expiry, or explicit null for a standing mandate. The worked example is 'a standing weekly mandate' (§1).

render_state_hash.description: §6.3, optional: 'Mandate and MandatePatch signatures optionally carry a render-state hash computed over the composited interface as presented.'

attestation_tier.description: §6.3, optional; 'with the software tier declared evidentially weak'.

$comment: PROFILE-DEFINED, collected: the deterministic serialization and hash encoding (§4.3); the commitment construction for commit(E₀) (§3.1); the embedding distance function and its range (§3.1); the taxonomy vocabulary (§3.1); the machine-interpretation vocabulary (§3.1); the predicate expression language (§4.2); the forced-supersession patch ceiling and the cooling-off interval (§4.4); Δ (§5.2); challenge TTL and caps (§6); the assurance-tier vocabulary (§6.2); the renderer identifier and the composited-interface canonicalization (§6.3). This repository ships artifacts only: no scorer, no evaluator, no consume authority, no renderer.

anchor.description: Independent evidence that a signature existed at its `signed_at`. OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED: routine verification can rely on a self-asserted `signed_at`, but dispute-grade evidence cannot, because a self-asserted timestamp is asserted by the one party with an incentive to misstate it. PROFILE-DEFINED: profile v1 anchors into the §5.2 transparency log rather than standing up a second log — §5.2 already requires 'cosigned heads or a witness network against split-view equivocation', which is precisely the property a time anchor needs, so reusing it adds a guarantee without adding an operator. RECORDED ALTERNATIVE: an RFC 3161 timestamp authority, which a §5.2 issuer-registry deployment needs instead, since such a deployment may run no log at all. Stapled at signing time, so dispute-time verification never depends on a service endpoint still being reachable years later.

log_id.description: Identifier of the §5.2 transparency log this signature is anchored in.

epoch.description: Log epoch whose cosigned head covers this entry — the same epoch space a supersession record advances (§5.2, §7).

inclusion_proof.description: Merkle audit path from this signature's leaf to the epoch head, ordered leaf-ward to root-ward, each sibling hash base64url unpadded. PROFILE-DEFINED: leaf encoding and the log's hash function.

hash.description: PROFILE-DEFINED hash encoding. Profile v1: SHA-256 over the JCS (RFC 8785) serialization, base64url without padding, prefixed with the algorithm name.

kid.description: Key identifier of the signing key. PROFILE-DEFINED: the derivation. Profile v1 uses `base64url(SHA-256(SPKI DER))` without padding — the unpadded base64url encoding of the SHA-256 digest of the DER-encoded SubjectPublicKeyInfo of the signing public key. The identifier is therefore CONTENT-DERIVED and unambiguous without consulting any directory; a key directory only RESOLVES a `kid` to its material and validity interval, it never defines it. REQUIRED, and deliberately not optional: evidence signed without a key identifier is verifiable only by trial-verification against every historical key, which goes ambiguous the instant two keys coexist. This field is NOT retrofittable — artifacts already signed without it can never be cleanly verified after a rotation, which is why it is present from the first commit. RECORDED ALTERNATIVE: an RFC 7638 JWK thumbprint, which is equally content-derived but fixes the key representation to JWK rather than SPKI.

alg.description: Signature algorithm identifier, JOSE/COSE name. PROFILE-DEFINED: the disclosure constrains no algorithm suite. Profile v1 admits exactly this set — ES256/ES384/ES512, the ECDSA suite AP2 v0.2 requires of its bindings; EdDSA (Ed25519); and RS256/PS256, which appear on deployed WebAuthn authenticators. A binding profile MAY narrow this enum but MUST NOT widen it without taking a new profile identifier. This member REPLACES the former free-string `algorithm`: a free string and a constrained identifier naming the same fact can disagree, and disagreement about the algorithm is disagreement about what the signature covers.

signed_at.description: The signing instant, RFC 3339 with 'Z' and second precision — the same timestamp form every other timestamp in this repository uses (PROFILE-DEFINED, decided; profile v1 takes no epoch-integer form, so that a validity interval and an artifact's `issued_at`/`expiry` are always directly comparable). This is the instant that key-validity intervals are evaluated AGAINST: a signature verifies iff `signed_at` falls inside the [not_before, not_after] interval recorded for `kid`, and a verifier MUST verify against THE KEY CURRENT AT SIGNING TIME, NEVER THE KEY CURRENT NOW. Rejecting evidence because its signing key was rotated afterwards is a bug, not a security property — planned retirement is prospective only, and evidence anchored before it stays valid permanently. A self-asserted `signed_at` is adequate for routine verification and NOT adequate for dispute-grade evidence; see `anchor`.

domain_separation.description: §6.2: 'domain-separated over audience, relying party, mandate family and version, rail, and protocol purpose'.

ds_tag.description: §6.2 domain-separation tag: the digest of the domain separator this signature is bound to, base64url unpadded. DISPOSITION (PROFILE-DEFINED, DECIDED — this is the choice the schema makes rather than leaves implicit): profile v1 carries `ds_tag` HERE, in the JSON body, beside the `domain_separation` components it is derived from, AND requires it to byte-equal the domain separator bound into the carrier's signed input — the WebAuthn `clientDataJSON.challenge`, or the KB-JWT `aud`/`nonce` under an SD-JWT binding. A verifier MUST recompute the tag from `domain_separation` and MUST compare it against the value bound in the carrier; a body `ds_tag` not reproduced in the carrier is NOT covered by the signature and MUST be rejected. The body copy exists so that evidence can be checked offline without a carrier parser; the carrier copy is what makes the separator signature-covered. Leaving this disposition implicit is exactly what §6.2's transplant attack needs in order to succeed, because two verifiers would otherwise disagree about whether the separator is signature-covered at all. RECORDED ALTERNATIVE: carry the tag ENTIRELY in the WebAuthn/KB-JWT layer and leave only the components in the body — rejected for v1 because it makes offline evidence verification depend on a carrier parser, and because body components carrying no tag invite a verifier to treat them as authoritative when nothing signs them. PROFILE-DEFINED derivation, profile v1: SHA-256 over the ASCII prefix 'MandateLifecycle/v1/transcript' followed by LP(purpose), LP(audience), LP(relying_party), LP(mandate_family_id), LP(decimal encoding of mandate_version), LP(rail), LP(binding_profile), where LP(x) is the uint16 big-endian byte length of the UTF-8 encoding of x followed by those bytes — length-prefixed with NO delimiters, because `relying_party` and `mandate_family_id` are attacker-influenced. The prefix MUST differ from the §7 nullifier prefix ('MandateLifecycle/v1/nullifier') so that a transcript tag and a nullifier tag can never collide.

anchor.description: OPTIONAL but RECOMMENDED — see the `$defs/anchor` description. Omit it and `signed_at` is self-asserted, which does not carry dispute-grade weight, because the signer is precisely the party with an incentive to misstate the signing time.
